selectionNote: 12 of 64 public repositories, chosen by reading the code. Left out: 2 forks, a repo where most commits are by other people, a duplicate build, setup and practice repos, tests, AI-builder scaffolds and an earlier portfolio.

projects.name: RideFlow
projects.tagline: Car-rental platform with role-based auth, an admin console and crypto checkout flows.
projects.summary: A Next.js 16 App Router build with NextAuth v5 sessions, middleware-protected admin and customer areas, a filterable fleet catalogue and an SEO layer: dynamic sitemap, robots rules and noindexed dashboards.

image.alt: RideFlow homepage: luxury car hero with a vehicle search panel for location and pickup and return dates

projects.problem: Renting a premium car online should take minutes, while staff need one place to run the fleet, reservations, content and payments, and private areas must stay out of search results.
features: Public fleet catalogue filtered by vehicle type, premium, seats, bags and transmission, with best-price and flexible rates.
Checkout with a crypto payment step (USDC, BTC, ETH, SOL). Wallet connection and conversion rates are simulated in this build.
Customer dashboard with bookings, account details and wallet tabs.
Admin console: fleet metrics, vehicle create and edit, blog publisher, crypto clearing and reservations.
Sign-up API route that validates input and answers 400, 409 or 201.
engineering: Role-based access in middleware: /admin/* requires the admin role, /dashboard requires a session, otherwise the user is redirected to /login.
NextAuth JWT and session callbacks carry the user’s role into the session.
Feature-sliced structure (admin, dashboard, fleet-catalog, home, blog), each with its own components, hooks, services and types; services are mocks ready to swap for a real API.

SEO built in: sitemap.ts revalidates hourly and adds vehicle and blog routes, robots.ts disallows private paths, dashboards export noindex metadata, and the root layout ships AutoRental / LocalBusiness JSON-LD.
projects.contribution: Sole committer on this repository (12 commits). The SEO workstream behind it is covered in the RideFlow case study under Selected work.
projects.skills: nextjs react typescript tailwind nextauth crawl metadata schema components rest

projects.name: SolarVue
projects.tagline: An interactive 3D solar system built with Three.js.
projects.summary: A React and Three.js scene with textured planets on animated orbits, a simulation-speed slider, a camera that follows any planet you pick, and live planet data from the Solar System OpenData API.

image.alt: Illustration of SolarVue’s 3D scene: the sun ringed by nine orbit paths and planets, under the app’s planet buttons and speed slider

projects.problem: Planet facts are easier to grasp when you can see scale and motion, not just read a table.
features: The sun, eight planets and Pluto as textured spheres, with orbit-path rings and Saturn’s ring.
Planets orbit and spin at relative rates, and a slider changes the simulation speed.
Clicking a planet locks the camera onto it as it moves; Free Look brings back drag, zoom and pan.
Each selection fetches live data from api.le-systeme-solaire.net: body type, moons, density, gravity, escape speed, radius, orbit and rotation periods, and temperature.
engineering: Orbits are computed every frame from sine and cosine of a time factor, so speed changes apply instantly.
Camera follow reads each mesh’s world position plus a per-planet offset on every frame.
OrbitControls panning is clamped to a bounding box so the view can’t drift out of the scene.

projects.name: CineDiscover
projects.tagline: Movie discovery and recommendations on the TMDB API.
projects.summary: A Next.js App Router app with trending and popular feeds, search, server-rendered movie pages with recommendations and per-movie metadata, and favourites saved in the browser.

image.alt: CineDiscover home: a featured film hero with rating, Watch Now and More Info buttons, a search bar and Trending This Week

projects.problem: Choosing something to watch means jumping between trending lists, search and detail pages. CineDiscover keeps them in one fast flow.
features: Weekly trending and popular movie feeds from TMDB.
Search by title.
Dynamic /movies/[id] pages with full details and recommendations.
A favourites page backed by localStorage.
Loading skeletons, an error component and a custom 404.
engineering: Movie pages are async Server Components that fetch details and recommendations in parallel with Promise.all.
generateMetadata gives every movie its own title and description, with a not-found fallback.
A typed API layer (lib/api.ts, lib/types.ts) wraps the TMDB endpoints so UI components stay presentational.
A useFavorites hook handles load, save and toggle with guarded localStorage access.
projects.skills: nextjs react typescript tailwind rest metadata components

projects.name: Heleph Coffee homepage
projects.tagline: A story-led homepage for a specialty coffee exporter.
projects.summary: A hand-coded single-page homepage, with sections on processing, single-origin coffees, zero waste, traceability, people and sustainability, and scroll-reveal motion that respects reduced-motion settings.

image.alt: Heleph Coffee homepage hero: the headline Discover the Magic on a teal gradient, with Discover the Magic and Explore Our Coffee buttons

projects.problem: The exporter’s story of origin, processing, traceability and people needed a homepage that sells the coffee, not just lists it.
features: Hero, values and a seven-part “magic” narrative from processing to sustainability.
A single-origin coffee collection and traceability section.
Partner and project sections with a closing promise and call to action.
engineering: One self-contained index.html (about 49 KB) using images from the company’s WordPress media library.
Sections reveal on scroll with IntersectionObserver, and a prefers-reduced-motion rule turns the transitions off.
Responsive breakpoints at 900, 767 and 640 px.
projects.contribution: Related to the modernised homepage I built in my role as SEO Specialist at Heleph Coffee Group.

projects.name: Forecastify
projects.summary: A framework-free weather app: it reads the browser’s location, calls the OpenWeatherMap One Call API and renders current conditions and a multi-day forecast beneath a live clock.

image.alt: Forecastify: a large clock and date over a mountain photo, above a row of daily forecast cards with night and day temperatures

projects.problem: Plans change with the weather. Forecastify gives a quick, location-aware read of today and the days ahead.
features: A live clock and date that update every second.
Current humidity, pressure, wind speed, sunrise and sunset.
Daily forecast cards with weather icons and night and day temperatures.
The location’s time zone, taken from the API response.
engineering: No framework: the DOM is rendered with template literals.
Geolocation coordinates go straight to the One Call endpoint in metric units, with hourly and minutely data excluded to keep the payload small.
projects.contribution: Sole author (14 commits), plus a write-up on LinkedIn.

projects.name: ALX Listing App
projects.tagline: Property listings and booking UI with Next.js API routes.
projects.summary: Airbnb-style listings with category tabs and filters, property detail pages with reviews, a booking page with an order summary, and API routes that serve property data.

image.alt: ALX Listing App home: search bar, category tabs and a lakeside cabin hero reading Find your favorite place here

projects.problem: A listings site needs fast browsing, clear detail pages and a booking step, all fed by one data source.
features: Home page with category tabs and filters.
Dynamic property pages with reviews.
Booking page with a contact and payment form, order summary and cancellation policy.
engineering: pages/api/properties/[id] returns 200 with the property or 404 with a message; reviews have their own route.
Shared TypeScript interfaces, plus reusable Card, Button and Pill components inside a common Layout.
projects.contribution: Built to the ALX ProDev Frontend program brief.
projects.skills: nextjs react typescript tailwind rest components

projects.name: CineSeek (PWA)
projects.tagline: An installable movie browser with a server-side API proxy.
projects.summary: A Next.js progressive web app with a service worker generated by next-pwa, a web manifest and icons, and a POST-only API route that queries the MoviesDatabase API with a key that never reaches the browser.

image.alt: CineSeek home: dark hero reading Discover Your Next Favorite Movie with a Browse Movies button

projects.problem: A movie browser should install like an app and keep its API key off the client.
features: Service worker and manifest via @ducanh2912/next-pwa.
Movie listing by year, page and genre.
engineering: The client POSTs year, page and genre to /api/fetch-movies, which adds the RapidAPI headers from an environment variable.
Requests other than POST get 405 with an Allow header.
projects.contribution: Built to the ALX ProDev Frontend program brief.

projects.name: Little Lemon booking
projects.tagline: React table-booking flow from Meta’s Front-End capstone.
projects.summary: A restaurant site in React with a reservation form (date, time, guests, occasion), available times updated through a reducer when the date changes, and React Testing Library tests.

image.alt: Little Lemon restaurant homepage with a Reserve Table button and a row of weekly specials

projects.problem: The capstone brief: let diners reserve a table with valid inputs and clear feedback.
features: Booking form with required date, time, guest (1–10) and occasion fields.
Available times dispatched to a reducer whenever the date changes.
Tests that render the app and open the booking form.
engineering: Controlled inputs with useState and labelled fields.
Routing with React Router 6; as the README notes, reserving a table is the only live feature.
projects.contribution: Capstone for the Meta Front-End Developer Professional Certificate.

projects.name: Monty interpreter
projects.tagline: A stack and queue interpreter for Monty bytecode, written in C.
projects.summary: Reads a Monty bytecode file line by line and dispatches 15 opcodes (push, pall, pint, pop, swap, add, sub, div, mul, mod, nop, pchar, pstr, rotl, rotr) over a doubly linked list.

image.alt: Code preview: the stack_t and instruction_t structs from monty.h beside the 15 supported opcodes

projects.problem: Interpret a small stack-based bytecode language with clear errors for bad files, unknown instructions and invalid operations.
features: 15 opcodes covering stack manipulation, arithmetic and string output.
Brainf*ck exercises in the bf/ folder.
engineering: An instruction_t table maps each opcode string to its handler through a function pointer.
Variadic error helpers (err, string_err, more_err) keep error codes and messages in one place.

projects.name: Sorting algorithms
projects.tagline: Thirteen sorting routines in C, with Big-O notes for each.
projects.summary: Bubble, insertion (on a linked list), selection, quick sort and Hoare quick sort, shell, cocktail, counting, merge, heap, radix and bitonic sort, plus a deck-of-cards sort, with best, average and worst-case complexity files.

image.alt: Code preview: a table of the repository’s sorting functions with best, average and worst-case Big-O, beside illustrative bars

projects.problem: Implement and compare classic sorting algorithms, and state their time complexity.
features: Twelve array and linked-list sorts plus a deck-of-cards sort.
A complexity file per algorithm, e.g. merge sort O(nlog(n)) in every case and counting sort O(n+k).
engineering: Insertion and cocktail sort work directly on a listint_t linked list; the rest sort int arrays in place.
Each algorithm’s best, average and worst case is recorded in its own complexity file.

projects.name: Binary trees
projects.tagline: Binary trees, BSTs and AVL trees in C.
projects.summary: Traversals, measurements, structural checks, rotations, BST insert, search and remove, and self-balancing AVL insert and remove, all built on one binary_tree_t node type.

image.alt: Code preview: function groups from binary_trees.h beside an illustrated balanced binary search tree

projects.problem: Build the core tree data structures from scratch and keep them balanced.
features: Pre-, in-, post- and level-order traversals.
Height, depth, size, leaves, balance, and full, perfect, complete, BST and AVL checks.
Left and right rotations, AVL insert and remove, and sorted-array-to-AVL.
engineering: One binary_tree_t node type, with bst_t and avl_t used for the BST and AVL APIs.
array_to_avl and sorted_array_to_avl build balanced trees straight from arrays.
projects.contribution: ALX Software Engineering curriculum project (15 commits).

projects.name: Interview problems
projects.tagline: Algorithm exercises in Python, plus one in Node.js.
projects.summary: Pascal’s triangle, lockboxes, minimum operations, log parsing, UTF-8 validation, N-Queens backtracking, rotating a 2D matrix, making change, island perimeter and the prime game, plus a Star Wars API script in JavaScript.

image.alt: Code preview: the N-Queens backtracking functions from the repository beside a solved 4 by 4 board

projects.problem: Practise the kinds of problems technical interviews ask, under time limits.
features: Ten Python exercises and one JavaScript exercise, each in its own folder.
N-Queens prints every solution for a board of size N, minimum 4.
engineering: N-Queens uses recursive backtracking with a diagonal-safety check.
Input validation with clear usage errors and exit codes.
